top_stories.title: Over 41,000 DHS Employee Records Leaked Online
top_stories.summary: Over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employee records were leaked online after allegedly being stolen from an Okta single sign-on system. The breach exposed both personal and work information of DHS employees.

top_stories.title: DHS: 41,000+ Employee Records Leaked Online, Along With a Map of What Each Account Can Open
top_stories.summary: A threat actor published a database containing personal and work details of over 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The leaked data reportedly includes a map of what each employee account can access, exposing access privilege structures within DHS.

top_stories.title: Massive Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers
top_stories.summary: A data leak has exposed records of over 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including approximately 10,000 ICE personnel. The data was reportedly taken from DHS's Okta login system and includes phone numbers, email addresses, office addresses, and reporting relationships.

top_stories.title: AI cybersecurity shifts to governing agents with Okta identity
top_stories.summary: Okta is positioning its identity platform to govern AI agents acting across enterprise systems, addressing the emerging challenge of non-human identities in cybersecurity. The approach focuses on establishing identity, authority scope, and authorization boundaries for AI agents operating on behalf of users.

top_stories.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
top_stories.summary: Microsoft is urging Entra ID administrators to migrate users from SMS and voice authentication to phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys. Microsoft has set a retirement date of February 2027 for SMS and voice authentication in Entra ID, after which users who have not migrated will face sign-in disruptions.

news.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
news.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirmed active exploitation, including CVE-2026-111357, a missing authentication flaw scoring 8.8 on CVSS. Attackers are chaining three flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure to achieve unauthenticated root access, directly impacting secure remote access infrastructure used in enterprise environments.

news.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
news.summary: SS7 and Diameter protocol vulnerabilities allow attackers to intercept SMS-based verification codes, undermining SMS-based MFA authentication methods. The article explains how these signaling flaws exploit inter-network trust relationships, directly impacting the security of SMS OTP used as a second authentication factor in many IAM implementations.

news.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
news.summary: CISA has reported that a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability is now being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw was patched earlier in the month, but attackers have begun targeting unpatched systems, raising concerns for organizations using GitLab for code repository access management.

news.title: Shufti ties AI agent actions to verified owners and permissions
news.summary: Shufti has launched Know Your Agent (KYA), a verification solution designed to authenticate autonomous AI agents and bind their actions to verified human owners and approved permissions. The product addresses agentic identity challenges where AI agents perform transactions like opening accounts or moving funds, requiring businesses to validate agent legitimacy, accountability, and authorization scope beyond simple access tokens.

news.title: Fake IT help desk callers got by on little more than names and email addresses
news.summary: Cisco Talos Incident Response documented multiple Q3 2026 engagements where attackers impersonated IT help desk staff via phone, email, and Microsoft Teams to trick employees into opening remote access sessions. Attackers used only employee names and email addresses to convincingly assume IT identities, with at least one incident resulting in ransomware deployment.

news.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
news.summary: Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann discovered 26,400 valid credentials exposed in public Gitee repositories after scanning 7.25 million repositories, with results reported on October 28. The exposed credentials were primarily API keys for cloud and AI services, all confirmed as still functional at the time of discovery.

news.title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees
news.summary: A hacktivist group published the work details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including names, titles, and phone numbers. The data was reportedly extracted from a login system, raising concerns about access controls and authentication security within federal identity infrastructure.

news.title: Session security, token protection, continuous access evaluation, and measuring what users ACTUALLY sign in with
news.summary: This article is part five of a seven-part series on Microsoft Entra ID, covering session security, token protection, continuous access evaluation, and passkey authentication. The piece explains how Entra ID issues tokens following passkey sign-in and addresses the security implications of token-based access persistence.

news.title: Massive data breach exposes 40,000 US Homeland Security employees
news.summary: A data breach has exposed sensitive information belonging to over 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The compromised data includes details on personnel in surveillance and human intelligence roles.

news.title: Personal data of 40,000 U.S. Homeland Security employees leaked in security breach
news.summary: A data breach exposed personal information of over 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, with the data published by leak site Distributed Denial of Secrets. The leaked data includes details on officials working in sensitive areas such as surveillance and human intelligence.

news.title: Leak website releases data on thousands of US Homeland Security employees
news.summary: A data breach exposed personal details of more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including identities, contact details, and job titles. Distributed Denial of Secrets claims responsibility for releasing the leaked data on their website.

news.title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
news.summary: A hacker stole personal records of more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, exposing names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations. The breach affects DHS staff including those in US Immigration and related agencies.

news.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — and Fraudsters Are Counting on It
news.summary: The article addresses how threat actors are bypassing technical security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering against help desks to gain unauthorized access. The attack vector targets identity verification and authentication processes at help desks, directly undermining MFA and access management controls.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across its Windows operating systems and other software. The company attributed the accelerated vulnerability discovery pace to AI assistance, while security experts noted organizations are struggling to keep up with testing and deploying the volume of monthly fixes.
